messages:
lee: Heads-up — customer C456 reported a sharp p95/p99 latency increase on our text-gen endpoints after yesterday's runtime rollout. They saw ~2x p99 for long-context workloads (seq=4096). Root cause looks correlated with the new kernel-selection defaults that enabled FlashAttention v2 on A100.

arjun: Can you paste the customer payload and any logs we have? Was this visible in canary?

lee: Repro snippet (from customer):
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "gpt-j-6b",
  "input": "<long prompt>",
  "max_tokens": 512
}
```
They provided traces: p95 went from ~120ms -> ~210ms, p99 280ms -> ~560ms. Canary metrics didn't alert because our canary traffic had shorter seq lengths.

maria: I reproduced locally on an A100 host. Micro-bench shows: before-change: p95=120ms p99=280ms; after-change (FlashAttn v2): p95=210ms p99=560ms. Toggle FlashAttn off and numbers revert to baseline.

kai: Interesting — I ran the same bench on a V100 and didn’t see regression. Looks A100-specific. Possible: new kernel compile flags + indexing path for flashattn causing extra mem copies for long KV lengths.

arjun: Can you share the bench command? I'll try in staging with different compiler flags.

maria: Bench command I used: `./bench --model gpt-j-6B --seq-len 4096 --batch 1 --iter 200 --device a100`
Perf summary (A100):
- baseline (legacy kernels): p95 120ms, p99 280ms
- rollout (auto FlashAttn v2): p95 210ms, p99 560ms
- flashattn disabled (runtime flag): p95 115ms, p99 250ms

kai: I dug into kernel selection logs. The compile changed default to `-march=sm80 -O3` plus `ENABLE_FLASHATTN_V2`. FlashAttn v2 uses a different tiling for attention which is great for short sequences but appears to thrash L2/cache on long KV caches. There's also a path that switches to SDPA for specific dims but the auto-switch thresholds are off.

lee: Customer is sensitive to p99 spikes. Short-term mitigation ideas?

arjun: Short-term: add a runtime toggle to force attention kernel to SDPA for models/requests with seq_len > 2048. That can be flipped per-model from the control plane without redeploying binaries. We can also expose an env var `RW_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL=sdpa|flashattn|auto` for emergency ops.

maria: Confirmed the runtime toggle works: set `RW_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL=sdpa` and re-run bench -> p99 drops back. Patch is small (config path overrides kernel selector). I'll open a PR.

kai: Medium-term: adjust auto-thresholds for kernel selector and add a micro-benchmarking job that runs nightly for seq lengths 512/2048/4096 on A100 and V100 variants. That will catch regressions.

arjun: Also need to revert the aggressive compiler flag change for A100 builds until we fully validate. I think `-DUSE_LEGACY_INDEXING` switch in the FlashAttn codepath might help — it avoids the new indexing algorithm that causes cache pressure. I'll try a recompile with that flag.

lee: Can we do a hotfix deploy to enable `RW_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL=sdpa` by default for the affected customer tenant(s) and stage a config for global fallback?

ops-bot: @lee created incident I-2026: flashattn-p99-regression; priority P2; assigned to eng-runtime.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued for runtime: build #2029 -> canary on 3 hosts, then 20% traffic, then 100%. ETA 30m.

maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2378 — adds per-model kernel override and env var. Added tests and a simple e2e that toggles kernels and checks latency.

arjun: I ran a compile with `-DUSE_LEGACY_INDEXING` + `-march=sm80 -O2` and bench looks promising: p99 down to ~260ms. Will run full perf sweep tonight and post numbers.

kai: Note: this regression only surfaces for batch=1 long-seq workloads. For larger batches, FlashAttn still wins. We should make selector consider both seq_len and batch size. Current heuristic is too naive.

lee: Action items: 
- maria: push hotfix PR and coordinate canary (blocking: infra sign-off) — target: roll in next 45m
- arjun: finish compile variants and perf data; propose permanent compile flag strategy
- kai: add nightly microbench job for seq len matrix + A100/V100
- ops: enable env override for tenant C456 as emergency mitigation

maria: Starting canary now. Will post logs here.

infra-bot: Canary started: hosts [a100-canary-1,a100-canary-2,a100-canary-3]. Config applied: RW_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL=sdpa.

maria: Canary perf after toggle (A100): p95=118ms p99=260ms. Traffic steady.

ops-bot: Tenant overrides applied for C456. They confirm latency back to normal in their next heartbeat.

lee: Great. We'll keep this thread open until global rollout and nightly job in place. Follow-ups: add runbook entry for "attention kernel p99 regressions" including commands below.

Commands / runbook snippets: 
- force SDPA at runtime: `export RW_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL=sdpa` then `systemctl restart redwood-runtime`
- per-request header (control-plane): `X-Redwood-Kernel: sdpa`
- bench: `./bench --model gpt-j-6B --seq-len 4096 --batch 1 --iter 200 --device a100`

lee: Thanks all — assigning to maria/arjun/kai to close after validation and nightly job created. :thumbsup:
